Definition: Assuming that what is true of the parts must be true of the whole. A quality of individual pieces is transferred to the group without justification.
Example: Someone reasons, 'Every player on this team is excellent, so the team as a whole must play excellently together,' ignoring teamwork and chemistry.
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'Each verse in this chapter is encouraging, so the whole Bible must never contain anything challenging or hard,' moving from a part to the whole too quickly.
HowToRespond: Distinguish parts and whole gently: 'That may be true of the parts — could we check whether it still holds when we consider the whole together?'
